title: Includes a Linux kernel header
message: <linux/...> and <asm/...> are Linux kernel uapi headers. The QNX SDP is not believed to ship them (guess; not checked against an SDP). Many uses are trivial (linux/limits.h, linux/types.h can often be replaced by POSIX headers); device-ioctl headers are not.
remedy: Replace each use with the POSIX/QNX equivalent of what the header supplied (types, constants). If it is a device ioctl header, the device needs a QNX resource-manager interface instead.
verify: verify against SDP: ls $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/linux and asm* before treating these as missing.

title: Includes a Linux-specific <sys/...> header
message: This glibc/Linux <sys/...> header is believed to be absent from the QNX 8.0 SDP.
remedy: Remove the include together with the calls it supports (see the per-API findings), or guard it with #if defined(__linux__) and add a __QNXNTO__ branch.
verify: verify against SDP: grep $QNX_TARGET/usr/include for the header.

title: Includes a Linux-only system library header
message: systemd, udev, D-Bus, SELinux, libcap and libnl are Linux system services/libraries; they are not part of a stock QNX image.
remedy: Isolate behind an interface and provide a QNX implementation (service start-up via the QNX service launcher, device discovery via resource managers), or disable the feature on QNX.
verify: verify against SDP: a port of the library may exist (qnx-ports); check before rewriting.

title: epoll event loop
message: epoll is Linux-only (known). QNX 8.0 is not believed to provide it (guess). BSD-style kqueue may be available through the BSD-derived io-sock stack and would be the closest analogue (guess).
remedy: First step: port the loop to poll()/select(). Closest analogue to try if the SDP provides it: kqueue/kevent via io-sock (guess; check <sys/event.h>). ionotify() with SIGEV_PULSE is native QNX, but it only works for resource managers that implement the notify handler for that fd; do not assume it covers sockets. For a pure resource-manager design use the dispatch_* framework.
verify: verify against SDP: sys/epoll.h and sys/event.h under $QNX_TARGET/usr/include before rewriting.

title: inotify file watching
message: inotify is Linux-only; no direct QNX 8.0 equivalent is known to this tool.
remedy: Options to evaluate: periodic stat() polling; kqueue EVFILT_VNODE if the SDP exposes sys/event.h for files (guess); or serving the watched files through your own resource manager so the writer notifies clients directly. Pick per use case.
verify: verify against SDP for any filesystem-change notification interface before choosing.

title: eventfd
message: eventfd is a Linux file-descriptor wake-up primitive.
remedy: Use a pipe() or socketpair() pair when the consumer needs a pollable fd; use a pulse (MsgSendPulse / SIGEV_PULSE) when the consumer already sits in MsgReceive.
verify: verify against SDP whether eventfd is provided in 8.0.

title: signalfd
message: signalfd turns signals into a readable fd; Linux-only.
remedy: Block the signals and consume them in a dedicated thread with sigwaitinfo(), forwarding to the event loop by pipe or pulse.

positive:
fd = signalfd(-1, &mask, SFD_CLOEXEC);
struct signalfd_siginfo si;

title: timerfd
message: timerfd is Linux-only.
remedy: Use timer_create() with a SIGEV_PULSE sigevent so the timer fires into your channel, or a thread blocked in clock_nanosleep().

positive:
int t = timerfd_create(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, TFD_NONBLOCK);
timerfd_settime(t, 0, &its, NULL);

title: sendfile/splice zero-copy calls
message: Linux zero-copy file transfer calls. sendfile() also exists on BSDs with a different signature, so a same-named call may compile but misbehave.
remedy: Fall back to a read()/write() loop (or mmap + write) behind a small helper; add a platform fast path only if profiling demands it.
verify: verify against SDP: some of these may exist with other semantics.

title: accept4
message: accept4() is not in POSIX.1-2017 (known). QNX 8.0 networking (io-sock) is BSD-derived (guess), so BSD-style APIs may be present and FreeBSD has accept4(), so it may exist on 8.0 (guess). Treat this as 'check the SDP header', not as a confirmed gap.
remedy: Check <sys/socket.h> in the SDP first. If it is absent: accept(), then fcntl(fd, F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC) and fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, O_NONBLOCK).
verify: verify against SDP: grep accept4 $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/sys/socket.h.

title: SOCK_NONBLOCK / SOCK_CLOEXEC type flags
message: Or-ing SOCK_NONBLOCK / SOCK_CLOEXEC into the socket type is not in POSIX.1-2017 (known). QNX 8.0 networking (io-sock) is BSD-derived (guess), so BSD-style APIs may be present; FreeBSD has both (recalled). May be a non-issue on 8.0 (guess).
remedy: Check <sys/socket.h> in the SDP first. If absent: create the socket with the plain type and set O_NONBLOCK / FD_CLOEXEC with fcntl().
verify: verify against SDP: grep SOCK_NONBLOCK and SOCK_CLOEXEC in $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/sys/socket.h.

title: pipe2 / dup3
message: pipe2/dup3 are not in POSIX.1-2017 (known). FreeBSD has both (recalled) and QNX 8.0 networking (io-sock) is BSD-derived (guess), so BSD-style APIs may be present, so they may exist on 8.0 (guess).
remedy: Check <unistd.h> in the SDP first. If absent: pipe()/dup2() then fcntl() for the flags (mind the small race window if other threads fork).
verify: verify against SDP: grep pipe2 and dup3 in $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/unistd.h.

title: MSG_NOSIGNAL
message: MSG_NOSIGNAL (suppress SIGPIPE on send) is not in POSIX.1-2017 (known). FreeBSD defines it (recalled) and QNX 8.0 networking (io-sock) is BSD-derived (guess), so BSD-style APIs may be present; it may or may not be defined on 8.0 (guess).
remedy: Compile-guard it: #ifndef MSG_NOSIGNAL / #define MSG_NOSIGNAL 0 / #endif, and signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) once at start-up (or pthread_sigmask in the sending thread) so a missing flag is still safe. SO_NOSIGPIPE is the BSD per-socket alternative (guess).
verify: verify against SDP: grep MSG_NOSIGNAL and SO_NOSIGPIPE in $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/sys/socket.h.

title: prctl
message: prctl is a Linux process-control multiplexer.
remedy: Map each option individually: PR_SET_NAME -> pthread_setname_np(); PR_SET_PDEATHSIG -> a parent-liveness check; PR_SET_DUMPABLE/NO_NEW_PRIVS -> drop (no QNX analogue assumed).
verify: verify against SDP: confirm pthread_setname_np signature.

title: CPU affinity (sched_setaffinity & friends)
message: Linux affinity API.
remedy: Use ThreadCtl(_NTO_TCTL_RUNMASK, &mask) for the calling thread (recalled QNX API; needs privilege). The mask is a bit set of CPU indices. Semantics are narrower: Linux sched_setaffinity(pid, ...) can target another process or thread, the runmask call applies to the calling thread, so per-pid callers need restructuring.
verify: verify against SDP: ThreadCtl runmask argument layout.

title: memfd_create
message: Anonymous in-memory file descriptors are Linux-only.
remedy: Closest analogue: shm_open(SHM_ANON, O_RDWR, 0600) then ftruncate()+mmap(): an unnamed shared-memory object with no name race (QNX supports SHM_ANON per its docs, recalled; guess for 8.0 flags). Fallback: shm_open() with a unique name followed by an immediate shm_unlink(), which leaves a short window where the name is visible (racy).
verify: verify against SDP: SHM_ANON in sys/mman.h and its behaviour on 8.0.

title: getrandom
message: getrandom is a Linux syscall wrapper. getrandom()/getentropy() may exist in QNX 8.0 (guess).
remedy: Check <sys/random.h>/<unistd.h> in the SDP first. Fallback: read from /dev/urandom (or /dev/random), which QNX provides (recalled), with a small helper that handles short reads.
verify: verify against SDP: getrandom, getentropy, arc4random.

title: Raw Linux syscall()
message: Linux syscall numbers (SYS_*, __NR_*) have no meaning on QNX (known: QNX is not a Linux kernel).
remedy: Replace each call with the libc/POSIX function it wraps, but check the semantics: pthread_self() is NOT a replacement for gettid (it returns an opaque pthread_t, not a numeric kernel thread id): decide what the id is for (logging, per-thread keys) and use pthread_self() only where an opaque handle is enough; a numeric thread id may need a QNX-specific call (check the SDP; guess). futex has no mechanical replacement: it is a redesign onto pthread mutex/condvar.
verify: verify against SDP: whether gettid() or another numeric thread-id call exists.

title: clone/unshare/setns namespaces
message: Linux process/namespace primitives (known); container semantics do not exist on QNX (guess: no namespace equivalent known to this tool).
remedy: Use fork()/posix_spawn() and pthreads. Isolation features must be redesigned with QNX process management (no namespace equivalent is assumed).

negative: static int clone(int a) { return a; }

title: AF_NETLINK sockets
message: netlink is Linux-only.
remedy: For interface/address queries use getifaddrs(); for routing-table changes evaluate an AF_ROUTE socket.
verify: verify against SDP: availability of AF_ROUTE in the io-sock stack.

positive:
s = socket(AF_NETLINK, SOCK_RAW, NETLINK_ROUTE);
struct sockaddr_nl sa;

title: Linux-specific socket options
message: Socket options that originated on Linux. Some exist on BSD-derived stacks with a different meaning or struct layout (TCP_FASTOPEN and TCP_INFO exist on FreeBSD; TCP_INFO's struct differs). QNX 8.0 networking (io-sock) is BSD-derived (guess), so BSD-style APIs may be present, so presence on 8.0 must be checked per option (guess). Not all of these are Linux-only.
remedy: Guard each setsockopt/getsockopt with #ifdef so it compiles away when the macro is undefined. If the macro IS defined, confirm the semantics and struct layout before relying on a same-named constant (TCP_INFO in particular).
verify: verify against SDP: grep each option in $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/netinet/tcp.h and sys/socket.h.

positive:
setsockopt(s, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_CORK, &on, 4);
setsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEPORT, &on, 4);

title: SO_PEERCRED / struct ucred
message: Peer credential lookup on UNIX sockets via SO_PEERCRED / struct ucred is Linux-specific in this form.
remedy: For an AF_UNIX socket port use getpeereid() or a LOCAL_PEERCRED-style getsockopt if the SDP's BSD-derived stack provides it (guess). MsgReceive's _msg_info (pid/uid of the sender) applies only if you move the design to native QNX message passing; it does not apply to a socket.
verify: verify against SDP: getpeereid() and LOCAL_PEERCRED in sys/socket.h/unistd.h.

positive:
getsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_PEERCRED, &c, &l);
struct ucred cr;

title: Linux-only open() flags
message: These open() flags originated on Linux. O_DIRECT also exists on some BSDs with other semantics.
remedy: Drop or emulate: O_TMPFILE -> mkstemp()+unlink(); O_PATH -> open(O_RDONLY) is not equivalent (symlink handling and permission checks differ), so check what the caller needs; O_NOATIME -> omit; O_DIRECT -> omit unless the SDP defines it with the semantics you need.
verify: verify against SDP: grep O_DIRECT, O_PATH, O_TMPFILE, O_NOATIME in $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/fcntl.h.

positive:
fd = open(p, O_TMPFILE|O_RDWR, 0600);
fd = open(p, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECT);

title: Linux-only fcntl commands
message: fcntl commands that are Linux extensions.
remedy: Guard with #ifdef; for pipe size tuning there is no assumed equivalent, accept the default.
verify: verify against SDP.

title: getauxval
message: Auxiliary vector access is Linux/glibc-specific (often used for HWCAP feature detection).
remedy: Use compile-time feature macros, or QNX's system page (SYSPAGE_ENTRY(cpuinfo)->flags) for CPU feature bits.
verify: verify against SDP: syspage cpuinfo fields on the target architecture.

title: sysinfo()
message: Linux sysinfo structure/call (memory, uptime, load).
remedy: Use sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) and, where the SDP provides it, sysconf(_SC_PHYS_PAGES) (guess for QNX); uptime from clock_gettime; the QNX system page (<sys/syspage.h>, asinfo) is the usual source for memory facts (recalled), so check there before sysconf.
verify: verify against SDP: sysconf names and syspage asinfo for memory totals.

title: mremap / Linux mmap flags
message: mremap and these mmap flags are Linux-specific.
remedy: Replace mremap by mmap new + copy/munmap old (or reserve address space up front); drop MAP_POPULATE/HUGETLB hints.

positive:
p = mremap(a, o, n, MREMAP_MAYMOVE);
mmap(0, n, 3, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_POPULATE, fd, 0);

title: Linux/glibc non-portable pthread calls
message: glibc _np extensions that may be missing (pthread_getattr_np may exist on QNX; guess).
remedy: pthread_yield -> sched_yield(); tryjoin/timedjoin -> a completion flag + condition variable with timed wait.
verify: verify against SDP.

title: Linux-only clock ids
message: Clock ids that are Linux extensions.
remedy: Use CLOCK_MONOTONIC / CLOCK_REALTIME; keep the Linux ids behind #ifdef CLOCK_BOOTTIME.
verify: verify against SDP which clock ids are provided.

title: Linux-only scheduling policies
message: Linux scheduling policies; QNX uses fixed-priority policies (SCHED_FIFO, SCHED_RR, SCHED_SPORADIC, SCHED_OTHER) and its own priority range.
remedy: Use pthread_setschedparam() with SCHED_RR/SCHED_FIFO and choose priorities for the QNX range; nice values do not map directly.
verify: verify against SDP: priority range for the target.

title: System V IPC
message: Availability of System V shared memory/semaphores/queues in QNX 8.0 is unclear: QNX has historically not provided them in the base system (recalled, unverified).
remedy: POSIX shm_open()/sem_open()/mq_open() for a quick port; for a request/reply design use native message passing (ChannelCreate/ConnectAttach, MsgSend/MsgReceive/MsgReply).
verify: verify against SDP.

title: FUSE filesystem
message: FUSE is a Linux kernel facility.
remedy: The QNX counterpart of a user-space filesystem/device is a resource manager: resmgr_attach(), iofunc_*, dispatch_create()/dispatch_block(). Map each fuse_operations callback to an io_* handler.
refs: QNX docs: Writing a Resource Manager

positive:
fuse_main(argc, argv, &ops, NULL);
struct fuse_operations ops;

title: Linux device node paths
message: Device paths are served by drivers; Linux names will not exist on QNX.
remedy: Take the device path from configuration and implement a QNX default; QNX devices are published by resource managers (for example UART ports appear as /dev/ser1, /dev/ser2).
verify: verify against SDP/BSP: the actual path for each peripheral on the target board.

title: Linux-only preprocessor branch without QNX branch
message: A Linux conditional on this line does not mention QNX. QNX compilers predefine __QNXNTO__ (and __QNX__).
remedy: Add an explicit #elif defined(__QNXNTO__) branch, or widen the condition if the code is POSIX-generic.

title: UNIX-domain socket IPC
message: Likely works unchanged (POSIX), listed because request/reply IPC is where QNX native message passing pays off.
remedy: First port as-is. If this is a hot request/reply path, consider ChannelCreate()/MsgSend()/MsgReceive()/MsgReply(); it gives priority inheritance across the call.
verify: verify against SDP: abstract-namespace sockets (leading NUL in sun_path) are Linux-only.

positive:
struct sockaddr_un a;
s = socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0);

title: /proc/self/exe
message: The Linux /proc/<pid>/exe symlink is not a QNX interface.
remedy: Use _cmdname() to get the running program's path.
verify: verify against SDP: _cmdname() semantics (may return argv[0]-derived path).

title: Linux /proc paths
message: QNX has a /proc, but it is a different interface (process address spaces, not Linux text files).
remedy: Replace with POSIX/QNX queries: sysconf(), getrusage(), the system page (<sys/syspage.h>) for CPU/memory facts, procfs ioctls (DCMD_PROC_*) for process info.
verify: verify against SDP: procfs layout on QNX 8.0.

title: Linux /sys (sysfs) paths
message: sysfs is a Linux kernel pseudo-filesystem; not assumed on QNX.
remedy: Query the real source: sysconf/getifaddrs for system facts, device resource managers for hardware state, the system page for CPU data.

title: /dev/shm
message: On QNX POSIX shared memory objects appear under /dev/shmem, not /dev/shm.
remedy: Use shm_open("/name", ...) and let the system pick the namespace instead of hard-coding the directory.
